subject: chemistry-1
question: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 each contain 6 protons, but carbon-14 contains 8 neutrons. Which term best describes the relationship between these two atoms, and why?

options.text: Isotopes, atoms of one element that differ in neutron number
Allotropes, different structural forms built from the same element
Ions, atoms of one element that differ in electron number
Isomers, substances with the same formula but different atomic arrangements

explanation:
Both atoms have Z = 6, so both are carbon; carbon-14 simply carries two extra neutrons (14 - 6 = 8 versus 12 - 6 = 6). Atoms of one element that differ only in neutron count are isotopes, and because their electron configurations are identical their chemical behavior is essentially the same. Ions differ in electron count and therefore carry charge, allotropes are different bonding arrangements of an element such as graphite versus diamond, and isomers are compounds with identical formulas but different structures.

ELI-10: The proton count is what makes an atom carbon, and it never changes without changing the element itself. Neutrons are different: they add mass to the nucleus but no charge, so you can add or subtract a couple and still have carbon. Carbon-14 carries 8 neutrons instead of the usual 6, which makes it heavier but chemically the same substance. Versions of one element that differ only in neutron count are called isotopes.
